messages.subject: The Hashmat class
messages.body_plain:
Hi Kylie,

I am currently using Cardinal version 1.6.0, and I have noticed that you have implemented a new class for storing the sparse spectral signals using the Hashmat class. Previously, I was able to convert the spectral data into a simple R matrix using "spectra(object)" or "iData(object)", however, this is no longer possible since using the "spectra()" method produces a Hashmat object and applying "pData()" on that produces a list of spectra whose elements are its non-zero elements i.e. they have different lengths. Is there still a simple way to convert the spectral content of an MSImageSet object into a simple R matrix?

Thanks,
Denis

messages.subject: Re: The Hashmat class
messages.body_plain:
Hi Denis,

Hashmat has been around since v1.0, so there hasn't been a change. Are your datasets the "processed" version of imzML? For that format (only), Cardinal must default to using Hashmat rather than an ordinary R matrix, due to the differences in how its stored vs. "continuous" imzML.

In any case, yes. You can simply do "spectra(object)[,]" or "iData(object)[,]". (The comma is actually optional as well.) Subsetting without indices will extract the full dense matrix as an R matrix. Depending on the size of the dataset, it may take some time to construct the dense matrix.

-Kylie

image(data.norm, mz=322.251, contrast.enhance="suppress", smooth.image = "gaussian", plusminus=0.01)
but 322.32 m/z value appears on the ion image.
Why?
Can I generate ion image for exactly needed m/z? Is Cardinal matching my m/z value to peaks maybe? Second question - can I move this m/z from ion image to different place, for example can it be displayed above ion image?
Thank you!
